item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00103","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C10","C25","C18"],"selected_candidate_label":"C10","confidence":0.94,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C10 is a strong drafting-template candidate because it addresses the same specialized communications-policy domain and supplies several concrete elements reused in the child: a presidential communications adviser located near the President, responsibility for communications policy and radio-frequency use, attention to governmental and nongovernmental requirements, interagency consultation, and protection of existing communications interests. The child appears to convert C10's temporary study board into a standing individual adviser with operational coordination and frequency-assignment duties. C25 and C18 contain some parallel organizational machinery, but their overlap is less distinctive and less directly connected to the child's telecommunications provisions.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"There shall be in the Executive Office of the President a Telecommunications Advisor to the President who shall be appointed by the President.","parent_excerpt":"There is hereby created a board to be known as the President's Communications Policy Board which shall be composed of a chairman and four other members to be designated by the President.","explanation":"Both establish a presidentially designated communications-policy instrument; the child adapts the board structure into a single standing adviser in the Executive Office."},{"child_excerpt":"Coordinating the development of telecommunications policies and standards applying to the executive branch of the Government.","parent_excerpt":"make and present to the President evaluations and recommendations in the national interest concerning (a) policies for the most effective use of radio frequencies by governmental and non-governmental users and alternative administrative arrangements in the Federal Government for the sound effectuation of such policies","explanation":"The child operationalizes the parent's communications-policy and Federal administrative-arrangements mandate."},{"child_excerpt":"Assigning radio frequencies to Government agencies ... and establishing policies and procedures governing such assignments and their continued use.","parent_excerpt":"policies for the most effective use of radio frequencies by governmental and non-governmental users","explanation":"Radio-frequency policy is a distinctive shared substantive responsibility, expanded in the child into assignment authority and implementing procedures."},{"child_excerpt":"telecommunications plans and programs designed to assure maximum security to the United States in time of national emergency with a minimum interference to continuing nongovernmental requirements","parent_excerpt":"study the present and potential use of radio and wire communications facilities by governmental and non-governmental agencies","explanation":"Both expressly balance governmental communications needs with continuing nongovernmental use, while the child adapts that concern to emergency planning."},{"child_excerpt":"he shall establish such interagency committees and working groups ... and consult with such departments and agencies, as may be necessary","parent_excerpt":"The Board is authorized to hear and consult with representatives of industry and the Federal Government ... All executive departments and agencies ... are authorized and directed to cooperate with the Board","explanation":"The child retains and strengthens the parent's interagency consultation and cooperation machinery."}]}
